authors: Nakagaki T, Umemura S, Kakiuchi Y, Ueda T
title: Action spectrum for sporulation and photoavoidance in the plasmodium of Physarum polycephalum, as modified differentially by temperature and starvation
why: The full action spectrum (relative sensitivity at each wavelength from ultraviolet to near infra-red) would set the slime view's colour weights, which are now invented from four peak wavelengths.

title: Blue-light photomorphogenesis in mushrooms (Basidiomycetes)
journal: Proceedings in Life Sciences (Springer), book chapter
why: Effective wavelengths and doses for cap and fruit-body formation in mushrooms would replace the fungus view's invented weights, now resting on one species tested at four wavelengths and on blue and red LED tests in two cultivated mushrooms.

authors: Rockwell NC, Duanmu D, Martin SS, Bachy C, Price DC, Bhattacharya D, Worden AZ, Lagarias JC
title: Eukaryotic algal phytochromes span the visible spectrum
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA 111: 3871-3876
why: Which colours brown-algal phytochromes absorb would decide whether the seaweed view keeps any red or far-red channel (the PNAS page failed to load).

title: Reproduction, growth and photosynthesis of gametophytes of Laminaria saccharina grown in blue and red light
why: Would confirm a blue-light row for kelps (fertility of the microscopic stage in blue light) and give doses; Springer refused the page with HTTP 429.

title: Blue light effects in marine macroalgae
journal: Proceedings in Life Sciences (Springer), book chapter
why: A review of blue-light responses across red, green and brown seaweeds; would confirm or correct the seaweed view's colour and direction rows.

title: Photomorphogenesis of reproduction in marine macroalgae
why: Which wavelengths control reproduction in seaweeds; would confirm the seaweed rows.

title: Light quality and sporulation in myxomycetes with special reference to a red, far-red reversible reaction
why: Which slime moulds need light to fruit, and whether red and far-red reverse it; would confirm or correct the Other slime moulds row, which rests on Physarum and on a 1950 citation of Gray (1938).

title: Photomorphogenesis of Marine Macroalgae
why: Red, far-red and blue responses across red, green and brown seaweeds; would show whether the red responses of brown seaweeds call for a red channel in their setting.

title: Potential sites for the perception of gravity in the acellular slime mold Physarum polycephalum
why: Whether and how the plasmodium senses gravity would decide whether the slime view gets the phone-tilt effect the plant and fungus views have.

title: A photoreceptor with characteristics of phytochrome triggers sporulation in the true slime mould Physarum polycephalum
why: The full paper gives the red and far-red responses of sporulation behind the slime view's Hunger row (only the abstract was read).

title: Spectroscopic detection of a phytochrome-like photoreceptor in the myxomycete Physarum polycephalum and the kinetic mechanism for the photocontrol of sporulation by Pfr
why: Absorption peaks of the slime mould's phytochrome; would set the far-red value in the slime rows.

authors: Ahmad M, Grancher N, Heil M, Black RC, Giovani B, Galland P, Lardemer D
title: Action spectrum for cryptochrome-dependent hypocotyl growth inhibition in Arabidopsis
why: The relative action at 500-530 nm in the full figure would turn the plant view's invented half weight for green into a measured one (only the abstract was read).

authors: Lange OL, Kilian E, Ziegler H
title: Water vapor uptake and photosynthesis of lichens: performance differences in species with green and blue-green algae as phycobionts
why: Backs a water row for lichens (waking from damp air or needing liquid water); DOI as given in the audited fungus sheet, and Springer refused the page with HTTP 429.

authors: Ballaré CL, Scopel AL, Sánchez RA
title: Far-red radiation reflected from adjacent leaves: an early signal of competition in plant canopies
why: The full paper gives the red to far-red ratios measured inside seedling stands; would refine the plant view's far-red estimate.

title: Phototropism of the Phycomyces sporangiophore: a comparison with higher plants
why: Side-by-side latencies and adaptation times for fungal and plant phototropism; would set the two views' pace on one scale.

title: Thigmomorphogenesis: the response of plant growth and development to mechanical stimulation
why: The founding measurements of how touch stunts plants; background for the plant view's Touch row.

title: Reflectance spectra of subarctic lichens
why: Lichen reflectance would show how a lichen's colour changes the light reaching its algae; background for the Lichens row.
